findings.title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) version
findings.body: Ruby has no method overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. The first definition is dead code, and Ruby emits a 'method redefined' warning. Any existing caller using the width/height form now breaks: with five arguments it raises ArgumentError, and with four arguments the height is bound to `opts`, so `opts[:allow_animation]` raises or misbehaves. Keep a single `downsize` signature and update every caller, or give the new variant a different name.

findings.title: Percentage dimensions break the animated GIF downsize path, so the loop silently fails
findings.body: The call passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` with the dimension string "80%". When the setting is on and the filename matches /\.GIF$/i, `optimize` switches to `downsize_instructions_animated`. That delegates to the gifsicle command `--resize-fit 80%`, and gifsicle's `--resize-fit` takes WxH, not a percentage. The command fails and `convert_with` returns false. The return value is ignored, so the loop runs all 5 attempts, spawning a process each time, and the oversized GIF is passed on unchanged. There is also no check or log that downsizing failed.

findings.title: Size check relies on the Tempfile handle after the file is rewritten externally by convert/ImageOptim
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` rewrites the file through its path using external `convert` and ImageOptim. The loop condition and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` depend on `tempfile.size`. If ImageOptim replaces the file (new inode) rather than rewriting it in place, the open Tempfile handle can report a stale size or read stale content. The loop would then keep downsizing needlessly, or the recorded filesize would not match the stored data. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` and reopen or rewind the file after modifying it.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` was `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and is now a constant 10MB for both images and attachments. Attachments are no longer checked against `max_attachment_size_kb` on the client. A site with a smaller limit lets users upload up to 10MB before the server rejects it. A site with a larger limit blocks files between the configured limit and 10MB ... and anything above 10MB, even though the setting allows it. The error dialog also reports 10MB instead of the real limit. The same hard-coded value is repeated in the 413 handler at line 246. A shared constant would at least avoid the duplication.

findings.title: API URL download limit changed from the site setting to a hard-coded 10MB
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` became `10.megabytes`. The download cap no longer follows site configuration. Sites that set `max_image_size_kb` lower now fetch up to 10MB of arbitrary data before it is rejected or downsized. Non-image attachments get the same fixed cap regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb`. This should be a named constant or setting.

findings.title: New auto-downsizing behaviour and signature change have no tests
findings.body: The PR adds a retry loop that rewrites the user's uploaded file, a new `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature, and removes setting-based limits from the JS validators. It adds or updates no specs. Untested cases include an oversized image being shrunk below the limit, the 5-attempt cap, GIF handling, and `max_image_size_kb == 0`. The existing JS utilities tests that exercised the setting-based limits are also not updated. The duplicate `downsize` definition would have been caught by a simple spec.
